text:
katie: Heads-up: us-west1 GPU pools hit sustained saturation for ~30m, lots of rejected requests. Not seeing autoscaler spike that explains it. Anyone looking?
sam: saw the alerts. preemptible pool churn + high tpm from short sequences. pulling admission logs now.
raj: timeline + which pools?
katie: started ~09:12, primarily gpu-pool-west1-preempt and gpu-pool-west1-shared. avg short requests ~6 tokens but many rejections. token buckets show drain -> negative then bounce. snippet:
```
[09:14:02] pool=west1-shared bucket=142 tokens=12 refill=30 cost=18 req_id=abcd1234 seq_len=4 overhead=14
[09:14:03] pool=west1-shared bucket=-6  refill=30 cost=18 req_id=efgh5678 seq_len=5 overhead=14
```
sam: that overhead fixed charge (14) is dominating for short seqs. our token_cost = overhead + seq_len * cost_per_token. for very short, overhead leads to high tpm consumption.
maya: two levers: lower overhead or add min_token_charge to prevent tiny requests from gaming the system? lowering overhead reduces accuracy of cost accounting. min_token_charge smooths but penalizes tiny requests.
raj: also worth checking refill smoothing. If we refill in big discrete quanta + many tiny requests arrive between refills, you get synchronized drain. consider EWMA refill rate to smooth.
sam: quick config idea: set min_token_charge=3 and ewma_alpha=0.2 for 30s smoothing. sample patch: 
```yaml
admission_control:
  token_bucket:
    min_token_charge: 3
    overhead: 14
    cost_per_token: 1
    refill:
      method: ewma
      alpha: 0.2
      interval_secs: 5
```
katie: that should reduce instantaneous drain. also noticed reserved tenants (dedicated capacity) were sometimes falling back to shared bucket when their dedicated pool hit transient errors. that's a bug: reserved tags not respected in bucket selection.
maya: if we isolate reserved buckets we need to cap how much of shared buckets are allocatable to bursts, otherwise shared drains and causes churn. propose shared_burst_cap_pct = 20.
raj: we should also recalc tokens_per_min by GPU capability. current model uses flat baseline which overallocates on older V100 nodes. formula proposal: tokens_per_min = floor(baseline_tokens * gpu_perf_factor * (vram_gb/16)). That maps token budget to hardware.
sam: good call. mapping tokens -> RPM is tricky: we currently divide bucket tokens by avg_tokens_per_req to get RPM, but avg changes with workload. use a percentile (p90) of tokens/req to be conservative in admission thresholds. e.g. rpm_limit = floor(bucket_tokens / p90_tokens_per_req).
katie: practical rollout steps?
maya: 1) immediate: set min_token_charge=3, ewma_alpha=0.2 (canary 10%)
2) fix reserved bucket selection bug in next patch
3) update tokens_per_min formula to include gpu_perf_factor and vram scaling (staged)
4) add telemetry: rejection_by_seq_len, bucket_level_by_pool, p90_tokens_per_req metric
raj: agree. i'll own numeric recalculation and give numbers for west1 pools.
infra-bot: alert created: cluster_scale_event id=cluster_scale_789, action=scale_up, initiated_by=scheduler @09:30
sam: rolling canary patch up: https://deploy/repo/commit/abcde set canary=10% for admission config. will monitor error rate + rejections.
deploy-bot: rollout started: canary 10% -> groups: west1-shared-preempt. rollout_id=roll_2026_176999.
katie: can you add a temporary Grafana panel for shared_bucket_level and rejections_by_seq_len? want to watch before/after.
sam: adding panel and alert: shared_bucket < 15% for >2m triggers slack ping.
maya: cost note: increasing reserved headroom or burst_cap increases tail idle GPU cost. better to pair this with packing improvements (bin packing short requests onto pinned nodes) to avoid capacity waste.
raj: I'll run a quick calc for tokens_per_min for v100 vs a100 and post numbers in ~20m.
katie: thanks. if the canary removes most rejects we keep, else revert. also prioritize reserved-bucket bugfix. :thumbsup:
